findings.heading: 2. File A already exists in the corpus, independently of this thread
findings.body:
Checked before re-researching (the "stale-cross-file pattern" this branch has hit repeatedly — see `[[cheap-check-grep-first]]`-style memory). All three intended File A nodes are already live:
- `de-edp-inventory` (`src/data/research/edp-inventory-regulation-479-2009.json`) — both editions (Dec 2015 Destatis copy, Oct 2025 CIRCABC copy) confirmed at source, `releases_per_year: 0.1`, resolved 2026-08-09 by the dropped-sweep pass, with dependencies to `eu-reg-479-2009`, `esa-2010`, and the two debt-statistics nodes below.
- `de-destatis-gni-inventory` (`src/data/research/esa-2010.json`) — `releases_per_year: 0.25`, minted 2026-08-08.
- `de-destatis-debt-annual` and `de-destatis-debt-quarterly` (`edp-inventory-regulation-479-2009.json`) — the two debt-statistics targets File A wanted.

**One real conflict**: Thomas's A1 ruling said "2 dated nodes is making most sense" for the EDP inventory; what actually got built is one node with cadence estimated from the observed interval between editions — the same shape used for the GNI inventory, and now the corpus's general pattern for this document type. Recorded in `EU/proposals/File-A-reconciliation-note_2026-08-09.md` as a flag for Thomas, not resolved by this session — splitting the now-integrated node to match an August 8th ruling made before the pattern existed would break consistency with the GNI inventory's identical shape, but that's a call, not a research finding.

findings.heading: 3. File B rebuilt from a fresh primary-source read, not from G.52.md's lost summary

Ireland (B1, held pending its 2018 PDF being opened), Luxembourg/Netherlands (colophon check: hosting Eurostat's own report, not their own), and France (clean miss) are recorded in `_dropped`, explicitly flagged as carried forward from `G.52.md`'s surviving prose rather than independently re-verified this session — their own JSON artifacts are the ones that were lost, and re-deriving conclusions already reasoned through once is not the same as re-verifying them.

findings.heading: 4. E: ESS explained, one modelling decision made, nothing else started
findings.body: Explained to Thomas conversationally: European Statistical System (ESSC = ESS Committee, the approval body named throughout the scoping doc). His ruling on the one open modelling question (SDMX 2.0 vs 2.1 as one node or two) is **one node, versioned** — the corpus should treat SDMX as a single evolving standard with version history in its description, not two separate nodes, which is the opposite of how the source catalogue itself lists them. Not yet executed — no SDMX node exists yet to apply this to; record the ruling for whoever mints it. None of the 8 candidate members (`EU/CatalogueOfESSStandards_scoping_2026-08-08.md`'s own suggested order: EBS business-registers manual, then seasonal adjustment 2015→2024, then temporal disaggregation, the precision/variance handbook, data validation 2.0, with GSBPM/ISCED researched from citing programmes not directly, EDAMIS skipped as a system not a publication) were researched this session.

findings.heading: 5. File C rebuilt and independently re-verified against EUR-Lex, not against Grok's lost summary
findings.body:
`EU/proposals/eu-legal-instrument-lineages.json`, 19 report nodes, 13 `supersedes` relations, 0 dependencies. Every repeal-clause claim was fetched directly this session (`curl` + HTML-to-text) and checked against the instrument's own Article text, not against Grok's characterization of it. Five chains, matching G.52.md's original scope: EU Financial Regulation (3 generations: 2024/2509 -> 2018/1046 -> 966/2012), Horizon Europe framework Regulation (2021/695 -> 1291/2013 -> 1982/2006/EC "FP7"), Horizon Europe Specific Programme (2021/764 -> 2013/743/EU, a separate chain), CAP Strategic Plans (2021/2115 -> {1305/2013, 1307/2013}, extended one generation further per C3), NDICI-Global Europe (2021/947 -> {466/2014/EU, 2017/1601, 480/2009}), and EU Recovery Instrument 2020/2094 (confirmed one-off, independently re-verified rather than trusted).

**Two open questions from the Decisions doc are now closed, one as a positive confirmation and one as a negative finding:**
- **C5 confirmed**: `eu-reg-2017-1601`'s title, supplied by Grok "from general knowledge" and flagged for confirmation, is correct -- "Regulation (EU) 2017/1601 ... establishing the European Fund for Sustainable Development (EFSD), the EFSD Guarantee and the EFSD Guarantee Fund" -- verified by direct fetch of the Regulation's own text (via a `CELEX:`-style URL, needed because the `/eli/` path returned a search-results redirect rather than the document for this and two other older instruments).
- **C2 closed as a negative finding, not a research gap**: NDICI's Article 50 repeal clause names only three predecessors (480/2009, 2017/1601, 466/2014/EU) -- the seven other 2014-generation external-action instruments (DCI, ENI, EIDHR, and four others) are named only in a financial-transitional context, not repealed. They lapsed on their own 2014-2020 MFF schedule rather than being superseded by NDICI. **Do not model a `supersedes` edge from NDICI to DCI/ENI/EIDHR** -- the source text does not support it. A refuted hypothesis, recorded as this project's convention asks.

**Two chains turned out one node deeper than G.52.md's description, found by reading the actual repeal clause rather than trusting the summary**: Horizon Europe's framework Regulation repeals *two* 2013 predecessors in the same article (1291/2013 and a rules-of-participation sibling, 1290/2013, not previously named), and CAP's direct-payments Regulation similarly repeals two predecessors (73/2009, the one C3 asked about, and 637/2008, a cotton-specific aid scheme not previously named). Both handled as one-to-many `supersedes` per D2's existing ruling. 637/2008's own title was not independently fetched -- flagged in the file's `_open_questions` as a lower-confidence node than the rest.

**One decision surfaced for Thomas, not resolved by this session**: the file uses a domain value, `eu-budget`, that is neither one of the three D1 already named (`research-innovation`, `agriculture`, `external-action`) nor present in `src/lib/types.ts`'s `Domain` union. The file's own `_import_note` flags this and suggests the existing `financial-regulation` value as a possible fit instead, without deciding. All three D1-approved domains also still need adding to the `Domain` union and to `Research.1.md` section 6's list *in the same commit* that imports this file -- confirmed by direct read that none of the three exist yet.

findings.heading: 6. E: 4 of 8 remaining ESS catalogue candidates researched at source; 2 correctly skipped; 1 genuinely blocked
findings.body:
`EU/proposals/ess-catalogue-standards.json`, 6 report nodes (4 catalogue members + SDMX + the EBS Regulation as a dependency target), 1 dependency. Each of the 4 documents was fetched and read directly (`pdftotext -layout` on the live PDF), not summarized secondhand:
- **EBS business-registers manual**: 2021 edition confirmed (KS-GQ-20-006-EN-N), and its own text confirms a real predecessor -- 'The updated manual has only 10 chapters compared with 24 chapters in the 2010 edition' -- resolving the scoping doc's speculation into a real cadence (0.09/yr, 11-year interval).
- **Seasonal adjustment guidelines**: found a THIRD edition the scoping doc could only guess at. It flagged 2009 as 'plausible... but not verified, do not assert it' -- this session found and fetched it (KS-RA-09-006), and the 2024 edition's own text confirms the full lineage: 'Following the 2009 and 2015 editions which were widely accepted and implemented, the 2024 revised ESS Guidelines...'.
- **Temporal disaggregation guidelines** (2018, KS-06-18-355) and **precision/variance handbook** (2013, KS-RA-13-029): both confirmed, both genuinely single-edition documents -- cadence left absent rather than guessed, matching Research.1.md section 4's 'preferred not required' rule.
- **EU Regulation 2019/2152** (the EBS Regulation), previously flagged in Research.1.md section 12 as unread, is now confirmed independently at EUR-Lex and wired as the manual's `methodology_depends_on` target.
- **SDMX**: minted as ONE node per Thomas's ruling, with version history (1.0, 2.0, 2.1, 3.0 Sept 2021, 3.1 May 2025) confirmed from sdmx.org directly -- note SDMX 3.0/3.1 are not in the ESS Catalogue itself but are included since the ruling treats SDMX as a continuously-evolving standard, not a catalogue snapshot.

**Two candidates correctly NOT researched**: GSBPM 5.1 and ISCED 2011, per the scoping doc's own standing rule for classification hubs ('do not research it by reading it. Its edges come from the programmes coded to it'). Not a gap -- a deliberate, previously-decided exclusion, applied rather than re-litigated.

**One candidate genuinely blocked**: Methodology for data validation 2.0, hosted on `cros-legacy.ec.europa.eu`, returned a DNS resolution failure to both a direct `curl` fetch and the WebFetch tool from this environment. Same class of access gate the scoping doc already documented for CIRCABC and ShowVoc -- needs a real browser session, not an agent's HTTP client. A v1.0 and v1.1 of the same document were found in search results but not opened either.

**EDAMIS** (catalogue member #12) was already correctly ruled out as a node by the scoping doc ('a transmission system, not a publication') -- not attempted, per that existing ruling.

findings.heading: 7. All three drafts promoted, validated, and imported -- corpus now 499/607/3
findings.body:
File B, the legal-instrument-lineages file, and the ESS catalogue file were all reviewed and imported the same session, after Thomas said "carry on with the drafts". Two real bugs were caught by the validator that a visual read of the JSON had missed:
- `releases_per_year: null` is not the same as omitting the field -- the validator rejects `null` explicitly ('must be positive when present'). Fixed across 23 nodes (19 in the legal-instrument-lineages file, 4 in the ESS catalogue file) by deleting the key rather than nulling it.
- Adding a value to the `Domain` *type* in `src/lib/types.ts` is not enough -- there is a separate runtime `DOMAINS` array the validator checks against, and it silently allows a typo'd or unlisted domain to pass the type checker while failing at runtime. `research-innovation`, `agriculture` and `external-action` were added to both. Also caught: the legal-instrument-lineages file used `jurisdiction_level: "eu"` throughout, which is not a valid `JurisdictionLevel` -- the corpus convention (confirmed against `esa-2010.json`) is `supranational`. And `relations` entries need `relation_type` (not `relationship_type`, which is `Dependency`'s field name) plus a required `evidence_url` -- both missing on all 13 `supersedes` relations, fixed by using each source instrument's own EUR-Lex URL as the evidence.

`npm run validate` and `tsc --noEmit` both exit 0 after fixes, run fresh in the cloud sandbox per the established procedure. Corpus is now **499 reports, 607 dependencies, 3 relations** (up from 473/605/3) -- `START-HERE.md`, `Research.1.md` section 1, and `planning/MISSION-TODO-2.md`'s header all updated to match, continuing the running pattern this branch has hit before (`G.75.md` Finding 3) of the count going stale within the same day it's fixed. All three promoted `EU/proposals/` copies moved to `_to_delete/` per that folder's own stated workflow; `EU/proposals/README.md` updated to reflect the promotion.

findings.heading: 8. G (2.9, Europe depth-pass leftovers): 2 of 3 items already stale, 1 genuinely researched and closed
findings.body:
Thomas said "tackle g" after the drafts were imported. G is OPEN-THREADS 2.7 + 2.8 + 2.9 (`G.75.md` Finding 1's table). Read 2.7-2.9 directly rather than trusting the secondhand summary this hand-off chain has been carrying -- the same discipline `G.75.md` itself argued for. Started with 2.9 (`[M]`, the smallest) and grepped the corpus before researching, per `[[cheap-check-grep-first]]`:
- **The Dutch Kadaster/BRK node was already minted.** `nl-kadaster-brk` exists in `nl-municipal-finance.json`, resolved 2026-08-09 by a sweep session that never cross-referenced OPEN-THREADS 2.9 -- the third instance this session alone of the stale-cross-file pattern (after File A and the corpus-count staleness). OPEN-THREADS 2.9 corrected in place.
- **Norway's municipal årsregnskap was genuinely open** -- confirmed by reading the actual `_dropped` entry in `no-government-finance.json` rather than assuming. Minted `no-kommune-arsregnskap` (Norwegian municipalities' own annual accounts, the primary document KOSTRA aggregates -- same category as the Dutch `nl-iv3-rapportage`), sourced by direct fetch of SSB's Kommuneregnskap statistics page (legal basis: Municipality Act section 16-1, reporting regulation 2019-10-18-1412) plus the corpus's own previously-verified KOSTRA veileder quote (22 February reporting deadline). Wired `no-ssb-kostra -> no-kommune-arsregnskap` (`uses_data_from`). The underlying budsjett- og regnskapsforskrift (2019-06-07-714) remains unopenable -- lovdata.no is robots-disallowed, the same limitation this file's own `_status` already documented for the Kommuneloven statute itself.
- **The UK leftover was already tracked, not new** -- `uk-local-government-finance.json`'s own `_dropped` already carries "a second council (York) also citing the CIPFA Code" as `deferred`. Not attempted this session; it is cheap-check-shaped, not G-shaped.

Corpus now **500 reports, 608 dependencies, 3 relations**. `npm run validate` and `tsc --noEmit` both re-run clean after this addition (fresh cloud-sandbox run, same procedure). Governing docs updated again to match -- the count has now moved three times in one session (473 -> 499 -> 500), which is itself the strongest possible illustration of cheap check 15's point about hand-typed counts.

**2.7 (AU, `[L]`) and 2.8 (beyond-Europe, `[XL]`) were NOT started.** Both are substantial, multi-source primary-research efforts in their own right -- 2.7 needs four previously-403'd NSW council Revenue Policy PDFs re-attempted plus Victoria's Valuation of Land Act 1960 and Valuer-General chain built to match NSW's structure; 2.8 needs Chile's SII avalúo fiscal (a fourth property-valuation tradition, per Grok Research Brief XI) researched first, then Colombia/Chile-FCM/Peru, then item 27's nineteen jurisdictions starting with the Crown Dependencies -- "still not_attempted across three sessions" per OPEN-THREADS' own note, now four. Neither fit alongside everything else this session did. Stated plainly rather than rushed, per this file's own Governing convention.
